bounded_conclusions: For the very short F-GC45 real-SWAP window, changing only the retained affine slope policy from +u_A/dt to zero or to the independently measured local corrector slope does not materially change the accepted physical state, corrector flux or published interface mass within the preregistered gates.
All three policies converged in two coupling iterations, so this fixture provides no evidence for a performance ranking among slope policies.
The head and residual paths differ, while the accepted physical solution remains invariant to approximately picometre head scale and 1e-17 m ledger scale.
Within this bounded fixture, the affine slope is therefore supported as iteration-response policy rather than authoritative physical mass.
This does not establish slope-policy invariance for stronger nonlinear response regimes or longer windows.
next: Use a stronger real-SWAP response regime where qualified evidence already shows u_A and local corrector response magnitude differ materially.
Repeat the same immutable-physics slope-policy comparison without changing acceptance or ledger rules.
Do not rank slope policies for performance until multiple response regimes are qualified.
